newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Nova raises bid for Techway.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Nova raises bid for Techway.

text.p: Nova Pacific Capital Ltd said on Thursday it will raise its on-market takeover offer for Techway Ltd to 38 cents a share from 30 cents.
The enhanced offer follows the share exchange counter-bid announced by Intellect Holdings Ltd on Monday of one of its shares for every 2-1/2 Techway shares.
Nova Pacific said that it had now acquired 18.7 percent of the issued capital of Techway, including substantially all of the shares from the two largest shareholders.
It said P.D. Jones, the founder and former chairman of Techway, supported the Nova Capital bid.
The bid compared favourably with the conditional scrip bid from Intellect, Paul Davis, managing director of Nova Pacific, said.
"Clearly the major shareholders have voted with their feet, and the Intellect bid can not now succeed as proposed," he said in a statement.

"With the Nova Pacific bid, Techway shareholders do not have to form a judgement on what the underlying value of an Intellect share might be, and can receive cash for their shareholding within the offer period," Davis added.

The new offer values Techway's 12.6 million issued shares at A$4.8 million. Intellect's scrip offer valued each Techway share at 39.2 cents on Monday and it will be adjusted to maintain this level if Intellect shares fall below Monday's 98 cents close.
Techway directors earlier on Thursday recommended shareholders reject the original Nova Capital offer.

Intellect designs and develops electronic payment systems, including smart card readers and cryptographic processors. It has been in talks with Techway for some months about Techway's WEB Australia division which provides Internet banking systems.
